content.text:
Perfect! Now I have enough information to resolve this ticket. The issue is clear:

1. The pricing-engine pods are crashing with a panic error (exit code 2) during startup
2. The panic occurs when compiling a pricing rule "BF-2026-STACKED" with an index out of range error
3. This is an application bug in the pricing-engine code, not a Kubernetes problem
4. Kubernetes is doing exactly what it's supposed to do - restarting the container according to the restart policy, which is why we see CrashLoopBackOff

The ticket mentions they haven't deployed pricing-engine since April but the crash started after 2pm today. This suggests the pricing rules (not the application code) changed. The rule "BF-2026-STACKED" is triggering a bug in the pricing-engine v4.11.3 code.

Let me update the ticket with my findings:

input.note:
Root Cause: The pricing-engine pods are crashing due to an application bug, not a Kubernetes issue. The pods are in CrashLoopBackOff because the pricing-engine v4.11.3 application panics during startup with exit code 2.

Evidence: Pod logs show a panic in /src/internal/rules/tiers.go:88 with "runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3" when compiling the pricing rule "BF-2026-STACKED" with 3 tiers and stacking enabled. This indicates an array index bounds violation in the application code [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-1].

Why Kubernetes is restarting: Kubernetes is correctly applying the restart policy with exponential backoff delays to the continuously failing container - this is the expected behavior [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#container-restarts-0].

Fix: This requires an application-level fix. The pricing-engine code needs to be patched to handle the stacked tier compilation logic correctly, likely in the TierTable.Lookup method. Contact the pricing-engine development team to:
1. Review the stacking tier logic in internal/rules/tiers.go around line 88
2. Fix the array bounds issue to properly handle 3-tier stacked pricing rules
3. Deploy a patched version of pricing-engine

Until then, you may need to disable or modify the BF-2026-STACKED rule in the rules-admin system to prevent the crash.
